Subject: Latency spikes — personalization requests piling in during flash sale

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing very large p99/p999 latency spikes during yesterday's site flash sale window (attached: trace bundle + dashboard snapshot). The pattern looks like a burst of personalization calls (many short prompts) that then hang for 10–30s on completion. This is causing cart abandonment on LB segments and is material for our Q3 launch.

Quick facts from our side:
- Window: 2028-06-23 14:50–15:10 PT
- Affected endpoints: /v1/personalize/generate (mostly short template prompts with user context)
- Symptom: completions stall at token N, client observes timeouts, then retries flood for same session
- Business impact: conversion drop ~8% in affected buckets, several merchants reported errors to ops

We've shared traces (lumina_trace_20280623.zip) and a screenshot of the Redwood dashboard. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? If it's on us, we will push adjustments; if it's on Redwood, we need an urgent mitigation plan.

Thanks — this needs exec attention if it is platform-related.

Alex
Head of Product, LuminaRetail

- Increasing concurrency cap for Lumina's dedicated pool by 25% to relieve queueing (Grace)

I'll come back with root-cause notes in the next update. Please expect a short window where some requests may be routed to the fallback model — should be functionally equivalent for the majority of templates.

Subject: Re: Latency spikes — personalization requests piling in during flash sale

Team — quick tech readout from initial triage:

What we see in Lumina traces:
- Bursts of many short requests (~50–200 tokens) that create a high volume of concurrent KV-cache warmups.
- KV cache churn: high eviction rate on GPU hosts serving Lumina pool; subsequent requests re-warm cache which increases tail latency on first N tokens.
- Batching pressure + per-account concurrency cap: requests queue up at the front-end until a free slot and then hit the host, but once they arrive they trigger long-ish kernel launches due to cache misses (head-of-line effect).
- Observed CPU-side retry amplification: client retries after 8s, which leads to spikes in concurrent outstanding requests and exacerbates queueing.

Short-term mitigations applied (already in effect):
- Raised per-customer concurrency cap by 25% (reduces queue length at front-end).
- Enabled lightweight quantized fallback (reduces per-request kernel cost by ~35% in our lab).
- Turned on request preemption for low-priority personalization requests (so long-running completions don't block new short calls).

Recommended follow-ups (next 72 hours):
- Add token-aware batching thresholds (avoid grouping many tiny requests into a single large batch).
- Implement adaptive KV-cache pinning for hot keys during flash events.
- Rate-limit client retry-attempts with a short jittered backoff suggested in SDK (coordinate with Lumina client team).

I've attached a light trace summary (included in the zip) and a couple of quick dashboard snapshots. We'll start work on the pinning and batching changes immediately; ETA for deploy to staging is 36 hours.

David Kim
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

Marissa

Subject: Exec readout + credit recommendation — LuminaRetail flash sale impact (summary)

Jonas / Ben — summary for your review and quick OK:

Impact: Lumina experienced p99/p999 completion latency spikes during a flash-sale window; conversion impact ~8% in affected buckets. We applied mitigations (raised concurrency cap, fallback model, request preemption, circuit-breaker).

Root cause (short): KV-cache churn + batching + client retry amplification produced head-of-line blocking in Lumina's dedicated pool.

Recommendation: Approve a one-time goodwill credit equal to 15% of June bill (estimated) and flag as SLA investigation (full RCA and SLA calc by 2028-06-26 EOD). The credit is intended to preserve the relationship while we complete engineering fixes.

If you want, I'll add this as a short line in the mutual action plan and wait for your approval before sending to Lumina.

Marissa Cole
